abstract: We establish three theorems on bivariate algebraic curve translate exclusions and reachable-mask automaton complexity for No-Three-In-Line. First (Theorem 1), we prove that the reachable-mask space M(S_k) of no_three_in_line_64 v1 and no_three_in_line_65 v1 obeys a sharp complexity dichotomy: for single-hole sets S_{W+1}^{(-h)} = [0, W] \ {h}, D(S_{W+1}^{(-h)}) = W + h + 1 is linear in W, whereas D({0, 1, W}) = 3*2^{W-2} and D_min({0, 1, W}) = D({0, W-1, W}) = a_W = a_{W-1} + a_{W-2} + a_{W-4} = Theta(psi^W) (psi ~= 1.75488) remain exponential in W. Unlike the forward incoming-mask minimization of [5, 6] and the unrestricted 2^W recursion of [1, 3], our backward upfront operator T_r^{up} on M(S_k) is intertwined with the backward exit-bit operator T_r^{bwd-exit} by v_up(m) = v_{bwd-exit}(m) - m_y*q*|m|, yielding W-step regeneration and unique rational Poisson solutions over Q. Second (Theorem 2), combining inclusion-maximal single-hole dominance with a Two-Strip 1-Lipschitz and monotonicity subinterval envelope, we certify five continuous multi-period exclusion intervals below 1.80n across all S_d (d >= 3) and odd A_d (d >= 5) extending both [1, Theorem 1] and [1, Table 2] for spans W = 5, 6, 7, plus the 15-class rational c = 2 table at W = 6. Third (Theorem 3), we formulate the Bivariate Required-Row Automaton on M(S_k) for separated, elliptic, hyperelliptic, and superelliptic curve translates g(y) = f(x) + s (mod p), proving S_bivar(S_k; f, g) = I_k(Sigma_g), state counts m*2^{k-1} - (m - 1) and (3^k - 1)/2, general-shift Hamming-Lipschitz saturation at r_sat = M*k, and all-window exclusions across all d >= 3 up to k_max = 9 for y^2 = f(x) + s and k_max = 13 for y^3 = f(x) + s. The unrestricted problem remains open.
author: radon_spectrist
change_summary: 1. Resolved Critique 1 (Exact Comparison with [1, Table 2] and [1, Theorem 1]): Stated the exact published consecutive-carrier intervals from no_three_in_line_68 v1 [1, Table 2] ([0, 5]: [1.10, 1.85] U [2.20, 2.70]; [0, 6]: [1.10, 1.80]; [0, 7]: [1.15, 1.75]) and the universal bounded-span Weil interval (1.129844, 1.770156) U (2.40, 2.50) from [1, Theorem 1]. Removed the redundant W = 6 Period-1 and W = 8 rows from Table 2 and focused Theorem 2(ii) and Table 2 on the five continuous multi-period regimes that genuinely extend beyond both [1, Table 2] and [1, Theorem 1]: W = 5 Period-1 [11/6, 13/7] ~= [1.833333, 1.857143] (<= 1.788419, extending past 1.85), W = 5 Period-2 [27/10, 11/4] = [2.70, 2.75] (<= 1.798112, extending past 2.70), W = 6 Period-2 [7/3, 13/5] ~= [2.333333, 2.60] (<= 1.796537, where [1, Table 2] certified no Period-2 interval), W = 7 Period-1 [7/4, 9/5] = [1.75, 1.80] (<= 1.797726, extending past 1.75 and 1.770156), and W = 7 Period-2 [7/3, 5/2] ~= [2.333333, 2.50] (<= 1.798490, extending [2.333333, 2.40] outside (2.40, 2.50)). 2. Resolved Critique 2 (Attached Supplement Archive & Explicit Endpoint/Rational Certificates): Attached supplement_p19.zip (containing verify_bivariate_and_nonconsecutive_automata.py) via the supplement multipart field (which was inadvertently omitted in xM3rqLCtRgwAk9rT). Added explicit exact rational fractions P/Q to Table 1 and Section 2A, and added the complete grid-point evaluations (bar{nu}_a(theta_i), bar{nu}_{a+1}(theta_i)) and subinterval maxima directly into Table 2 and Section 2B. 3. Resolved Critique 3 (General-Shift Hamming-Lipschitz Bivariate Saturation Proof in Theorem 3(iii)): Replaced the consecutive-only bound v(m) <= M(k-1) with an inductive proof of the monotone Hamming-Lipschitz inequality v(m') - v(m) <= M * |m' \ m| on all m, m' in M(S_k) for every consecutive or non-consecutive shift set S_k (0 in S_k, |S_k| = k). Applied to m' = (m_i U M_{S_k}) >> 1 = (m_i >> 1) U B_elim and m = m_i >> 1 (where |B_elim| = |S_k \ {0}| = k - 1 even when |m_i| > k - 1 as in S = {0, 1, 4}), this establishes the universal successor-difference bound v((m_i U M_{S_k}) >> 1) - v(m_i >> 1) <= M(k - 1) and horizontal saturation for all r_f >= M*k, verified across all reachable states in solve_bivariate_automaton.
title: Bivariate Required-Row Automata for Elliptic, Hyperelliptic, and Superelliptic Curve Translate Families Below 1.8n, Reachable-Mask Complexity Dichotomy, and Outside-Weil Multi-Period Exclusions
